Hi Liam,

Appreciate the diagram and ruleset. Quick answers up front and then a proposed next step:

- Control plane: Redwood supports two modes for private deployments — co-located control plane inside a customer-managed VPC (preferred for low-latency admin operations) or a remote control plane over a mutually authenticated control channel. Both are supported; we typically recommend in-VPC control plane unless your security policy forbids host-based control components.

- Egress: standard pattern is to separate telemetry and inference egress. Telemetry (metrics/traces) can go through a dedicated telemetry NAT with restricted endpoints; inference egress should be routed via an application NAT/egress gateway that enforces ACLs. We can provide our recommended iptables/NAT templates and an ingress/egress matrix.

- Cert rotation / KMS: we integrate with customer KMS for root secrets and use mTLS for node-to-node trust. Rotation is handled by the control plane with hooks for operator approval; we can share a runbook snippet.

Proposed next step: Aditya will draft a schematic showing the control/data-plane boundary and a short runbook snippet. Can we schedule a 30-min call Tuesday 11/17 10:30 PT to walk the schematic?

-Jasmine

Liam / team,

Attaching a draft schematic that shows: control plane (API server, auth broker, KMS connector) running in a customer-managed management subnet; inference nodes in isolated compute subnets with a per-tenant overlay network. Key notes inline:

- Control plane endpoints: HTTPS (443) + mTLS for node registration. Recommend OOB management CIDR for operator access and BGP session for on-prem edge where applicable.
- KV cache and model assets: cached locally on inference nodes; model pulls over an authenticated artifact service that is restricted to a signed URL with short TTLs.
- Egress: two-stage NAT. Telemetry -> telemetry-NAT -> restricted telemetry endpoints (Prometheus/OTel ingest). Inference egress -> app-egress gateway with IP allowlist.
- KMS: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via PKCS11 for root key material. We provide a rotation orchestration job that stages keys and rotates node-level certs with a canary rollout.

Hi all,

Thanks for the review notes, Liam. Short answers and an action list below.

Minimum control-plane egress (for a dedicated management VPC):
- outbound HTTPS (443) to: artifact-service.redwood-inference.example.com (model pulls)
- outbound mTLS to: auth-broker.redwood-inference.example.com (node registration)
- NTP (udp/123) to customer-designated time sources or internal NTP
- to KMS endpoint (if using cloud KMS) or to the HSM gateway (customer-hosted)

Impact of DPI/egress inspection:
- Deep packet inspection that terminates TLS will break node mutual-auth unless inspection is configured to forward original client cert headers or is explicitly bypassed for mTLS sessions. We recommend an allowlist for mTLS destination IPs and ports at the appliance so node-to-controlplane TLS is not intercepted.

Rotation timeline & rollback (summary):
- Stage: upload new key material to KMS / HSM (T=0)
- Canary rotate: select 2% of nodes -> issue new node certs (T+30m)
- Monitor: health checks and telemetry (T+30-90m)
- Gradual ramp to 100% (T+4h)
- Rollback: revoke new certs via control plane and re-issue previous certs from KMS snapshot (if health regressions are detected within 30m)

Action items:
1) Jasmine / Aditya: produce a minimal egress ACL list (we'll attach to the SOC/arch packet) — target: EOD 11/20.
2) Acme: confirm whether DPI appliance can bypass mTLS destinations or provide a proxy header contract.
3) Schedule a 30-min acceptance call (Jasmine to send calendar invite).
